extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and administrators preparing NIH grant applications involving human subjects (including clinical trials) and reviewers of those applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing the human subjects protections portions of NIH grant applications, including required forms, review criteria (risk, protections, benefits, importance, monitoring), inclusion plans, and IRB/assurance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Framework (45 CFR Part 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHS regulations for the protection of human subjects in 45 CFR Part 46 provide a framework based on established, internationally recognized ethical principles to safeguard the rights and welfare of individuals who participate in research supported by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the legal/ethical baseline reviewers and applicants must follow; underpins all other review considerations for human subjects protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk to Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk Category (e.g., research not involving more than minimal risk); Identification of all risks (physical, psychological, social, economic, legal); Likelihood and severity of each risk; Special protections for vulnerable populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether all relevant risks have been identified and characterized (type, likelihood, severity) and whether additional safeguards are described for vulnerable groups. Examples of risk types are physical, psychological, social, economic, and legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Protection Against Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruitment and informed consent procedures; Plan to protect privacy and confidentiality; Data management and security plans; Plan to address adverse events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposed procedures (recruitment, consent, privacy/confidentiality protections, data security) appropriately mitigate identified risks and whether there are clear plans for identifying and responding to adverse events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Benefits of the Proposed Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the knowledge to be gained; Direct benefits to subjects (if any); Generalizable benefits to society; Risk-benefit relationship is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider both direct and societal benefits, and whether the benefits justify the risks. The importance of the knowledge and likelihood that the research will yield it factor into the risk-benefit determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of Knowledge to be Gained
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance to the field; Value to society; Justification for research with these subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how the proposed study advances scientific understanding or public health and whether the chosen subject population is appropriate for achieving that knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring (for Clinical Trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of monitoring plan; Independent DSMB if needed; Stopping rules; Reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials, reviewers examine whether monitoring plans (including independent Data and Safety Monitoring Boards when appropriate), pre-specified stopping rules, and reporting procedures are sufficient to protect participants and preserve study integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Form: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information
rubrics_metrics.description: All projects proposing human subjects research, either exempt or non-exempt, including those proposing clinical trials, must complete the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of this form is mandatory; reviewers will use information submitted on this form as part of their evaluation of human subjects protections and clinical trial elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects Section (application content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must describe: Proposed involvement of human subjects; Assessment of risk; Steps taken to protect subjects from risk; Potential benefits from study to subjects and others; Importance of the knowledge to be gained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrative section must explicitly address each listed element so reviewers can judge adequacy of protections and ethical justification. Be specific about procedures, safeguards, and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan must describe: Inclusion of women, children, and minorities in the research; Anticipated enrollment figures table; Justification for any exclusions; Outreach and recruitment strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether plans meet NIH inclusion policies, provide realistic enrollment projections (via an enrollment table), justify exclusions, and include concrete strategies for recruiting diverse participant populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB and Institutional Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient institution must ensure all institutions engaged in research have a current, approved Federal Wide Assurance (FWA); Must obtain certification of approval by an IRB registered with OHRP for all nonexempt research before research may begin; Single IRB (sIRB) policy applies to multi-site non-exempt human subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and compliance requirements: ensure FWAs are in place, obtain IRB approval prior to initiation of nonexempt research, and follow NIH sIRB policy for multi-site studies. Reviewers and program staff may verify these certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Across the Lifespan Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects inclusion of: Women; Members of racial and ethnic minority groups; Children (per Inclusion of Children in Research policy); Older adults (per Inclusion Across the Lifespan policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should design studies and inclusion justifications consistent with NIH policies that promote representation across sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and age, unless a valid justification for exclusion is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Definition of Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A research study in which one or more human subjects are prospectively assigned to one or more interventions to evaluate the effects of those interventions on health-related biomedical or behavioral outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether a proposed project qualifies as a clinical trial for purposes of reporting, forms, inclusion policies, and data and safety monitoring expectations.
